title: Telemetry Forwarder: reconciliation API and robust delivery model for SIEM/Datadog/Splunk
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a resilient telemetry forwarder component and a reconciliation (replay/query) API so downstream SIEM and observability vendors (Splunk, Datadog, customer webhooks) receive audit events with clear delivery guarantees. This ticket scopes the delivery model, idempotency semantics, reconcilation surface, observability signals, and the operational playbook for incident reconciliation.
background: Customers need strong assurances for audit event delivery: ordered delivery where required, at-least-once semantics with bounded duplication, and a simple mechanism to reconcile gaps with destination systems. Existing connectors retry aggressively but lack a customer-visible reconciliation API and per-tenant delivery checkpoints. Previous tickets focused on webhook retries and DLQ mechanics; this work standardizes a reconciler + buffering model across SIEM integrations.
scope: In scope: event sequence IDs, per-tenant checkpoints, signed webhook payloads, in-flight buffer limits, exponential backoff with jitter, DLQ policy to object storage, reconciliation API (query by tenant/time/seq-range), reconciliation tooling (replay and dry-run), runtime metrics and alerts. Out of scope: vendor-specific SDKs beyond canonical JSON mapping, premium SLA contracts for Dedicated customers (handled separately).
proposed_solution: 1) Producer side: attach monotonic per-tenant sequence_id and event_id (UUIDv7) to each audit event before handoff to forwarder. 2) Forwarder core: durable, ordered per-tenant queues (Redis Streams for short-term bursts + S3-backed overflow snapshots) with a configurable window (default 72h). 3) Delivery semantics: default is at-least-once with idempotency enforced by destination idempotency keys (event_id) and dedupe at redelivery boundary. 4) Retries and DLQ: exponential backoff up to N attempts (configurable per destination), then persist to tenant-specific DLQ bucket/path with metadata for manual or automated replay. 5) Reconciliation API: HTTP endpoints to list gaps by seq ranges, request replays (dry-run or live), and fetch archived payloads. 6) Observability: per-tenant delivery lag histogram, retry rate, DLQ rate, recent-failure histograms, and reconciliation API usage telemetry. 7) Security: HMAC-signed webhooks (rotating keys via KMS), TLS, destination ACLs, and audit logs for replay operations. 8) Testing: end-to-end integration harness against Splunk/Datadog test endpoints and a synthetic SIEM to validate ordering and dedupe under burst load.

acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant sequence_id is present on every forwarded audit event and monotonically increasing for that tenant (verified in integration test)
Delivery SLO: 99.9% of events acknowledged by vendor test endpoints within 30s under baseline load
Duplicate rate after dedupe < 0.01% in replay scenarios (measured in integration run)
Reconciliation API can report gaps for any tenant/time-range and successfully replay archived events to a test endpoint
DLQ items include full envelope + failure metadata and are replayable via reconciler
Observability: dashboards show delivery lag, retry counts, DLQ rate and provide alerting thresholds
Security: HMAC signing and KMS key rotation demoed; all replay operations are audited
risks: High-volume tenants may cause large Redis Streams growth — mitigated by S3 overflow and per-tenant quotas
Replay storms: accidental replay could overwhelm vendor endpoints — mitigated by throttled replay and dry-run option
Idempotency boundary differences with vendor endpoints (some vendors do not provide idempotent writes) — mitigation: best-effort dedupe + explicit replay agreements in docs
Data residency concerns for archive buckets — mitigation: per-tenant region-aware bucket selection and opt-out for archive
decisions: Use event_id (UUIDv7) + monotonic per-tenant sequence_id as canonical delivery contract
Use Redis Streams for low-latency queueing + S3 for overflow/archival rather than a single Kafka cluster to reduce operational footprint
Expose reconcilation API with explicit throttles and dry-run mode by default
Default delivery semantics: at-least-once with explicit replay rather than attempting strong exactly-once across vendor boundaries
